Beállítom Az országban először a Magyar Természetjáró Szövetség online felületein, köztük a Kéktúra hivatalos mobilappjának térképén vált nyilvánosan és jogszerűen elérhetővé a védett és fokozottan védett területek aktuális rétege – írta közleményben a szervezet. Lapunk pont egy éve adott hírt arról, hogy nem nyilvánosak a fokozottan védett természeti területek határai , de fizethet, aki tudtán kívül odatéved. A térképadatok ugyan már akkor is megvoltak az ország turistaút-hálózatát kezelő Magyar Természetjáró Szövetségnél, de bármennyire is szerették volna, nem hozhatták nyilvánosságra azokat, mert az adatgazda Agrárminisztérium nem engedte. A Telex ezért közérdekűadat-igénylési eljárást indított, és az adatvédelmi hatósághoz fordult a nyilvánvaló közérdek megsértése miatt. Az Agrárminisztérium először egy elnagyolt, használhatatlan térképállományt küldött, de a kormányváltás után megkaptuk a kért vektoros adatokat is azzal, hogy azok még több szükséges jogszabály-módosítás miatt jogi és térképészeti felülvizsgálat alatt állnak, azaz akár néhány napon belül is változhatnak. Javasolták az úgynevezett WMS (Web Map Service) szolgáltatás igénybevételét, ami a folyamatosan frissített adatokat mutatja. Ám azt hiába igényeltük, eddig még nem kaptuk meg. Amint megérkezik, eredeti terveink szerint továbbítjuk az ingyenes OpenStreetMap önkéntes szerkesztőinek, hogy ne csak a Kéktúra appban, hanem az összes túratérkép-alkalmazásban elérhetők legyenek a fontos határok. A fokozottan védett területek határainak ismerete az MTSZ szerint azért lényeges, mert bár a természetvédelmi törvény rendelkezik a védett és fokozottan védett természeti területek látogatásának szabályairól, rögzítve, hogy az utóbbiakon engedély nélkül tilos elhagyni a jelzett turistautakat és tanösvényeket, ezeket a területeket eddig jogszerűen nem lehetett nyilvánosan elérhetővé tenni a digitális térképeken. Így a túrázók az utak mentén kihelyezett táblákról értesülhettek róla, hogy beléptek egy fokozottan védett területre, előre azonban nem tájékozódhattak ezekről, ami megnehezítette a tervezést, ráadásul a nem jelzett utak mellett általában még táblák sincsenek. Ez különösen a manapság egyre divatosabb vadkempingezés szempontjából idézett elő konfliktushelyzeteket, fokozottan védett területen ugyanis – mivel a turistautakról, tanösvényekről tilos letérni – sátrazni, bivakolni sem legális. Eddig az MTSZ is csak belső használatra, a mintegy 18 ezer kilométer összhosszúságú országos turistaút-hálózat karbantartásának menedzseléséhez kapta meg a védett természeti területek fedvényeinek munkaállományát, és évek óta lobbiztak azért, hogy ezeket nyilvánosságra is hozhassák. A szervezet szerint ez a túrázók és a természetvédelem közös érdeke, hiszen így könnyebbé válik a szabályok betartása, illetve betartatása is, és így segíthetik a kirándulókat a természetkárosítás és a természetvédelmi bírságok elkerülésében. Rózsaszínnel láthatók a védett, lilával pedig a fokozottan védett természeti területek – Forrás: MTSZ Mivel az állományokat negyedévente frissíteni fogja az MTSZ, a változások miatti elavulásuktól sem kell tartani. A Kéktúra app legfrissebb verziójában jelenleg rózsaszínnel láthatók a védett, lilával pedig a fokozottan védett természeti területek – ezeket a fedvényeket a rétegválasztóval lehet ki- és bekapcsolni. Ennek az előnyeit nemcsak a kéktúrázók élvezhetik, hiszen országos lefedettségű, offline használatra lementhető turistatérképe, túratervezője és túranyilvántartója révén az app bármilyen túrázáshoz jól használható. A területek megjelennek továbbá az MTSZ más publikus online térképein, köztük az MTSZ-térképportálon és az mtsz.org turistaút-nyilvántartásában, kiválasztható módon. Photograph: Hannibal Hanschke/EPA Germany Friedrich Merz vows to stay in office after CDU ‘disaster’ in German state elections Far-right AfD wins in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania and leftwing Die Linke on course for victory in Berlin Deborah Cole in Berlin Sun 20 Sep 2026 14.33 EDT Last modified on Sun 20 Sep 2026 15.23 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Germany’s embattled chancellor, Friedrich Merz , has vowed to stay in office and fight for future-proofing economic changes despite heavy losses for his conservatives in two state elections, one to the far right and the other to a leftwing party. Preliminary results indicated Merz’s Christian Democratic Union (CDU) tallied just over the 5% threshold to enter the state parliament in the coastal region of Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, its worst-ever state score, which he called a “disaster”. The anti-immigration, Kremlin-friendly Alternative für Deutschland (AfD) party extended a streak of strong showings by coming in first in the former communist region with nearly 38%, more than doubling its previous score. In the capital, Berlin, one of Germany’s 16 federal states, the far-left Die Linke looked on course to win with about 25% of the vote, ahead of the incumbent CDU by a five-point margin. The AfD made headway there too, with a clear double-digit result. The deeply unpopular Merz has been fighting for his political survival after a humiliating series of setbacks with voters this year. Speculation about his ability to hold on as chancellor reached fever pitch after Saxony-Anhalt state’s AfD chapter routed the CDU with a record 44% for the party in an election two weeks ago. The Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania result marked the third time the AfD has emerged as the strongest party in a region, although the party seemed likely to remain shut out of power in the state because of a “firewall” of non-cooperation agreed by the other main parties. In a rare speech on a state election night, Merz admitted the CDU had been bitterly deprived of “tailwinds from Berlin” in both of Sunday’s races. But he said he would remain chancellor and party chair and continue a reform drive on fronts including taxes, healthcare, pensions and reducing bureaucracy. Merz said the German economy was facing “profound upheaval”, while public discourse had become “harsher and more irreconcilable”. “Trust in our country’s institutions is waning and is being actively undermined by radical parties on both the left and the right,” he said. But he added: “Germany is capable of reform. I would even go so far as to say that these reforms are the antidote to the poison of authoritarianism, which is penetrating ever deeper into our society as the fascination with authoritarianism grows.” View image in fullscreen The AfD’s co-chair, Tino Chrupalla, react as he hears the first results of the Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania state election in Schwerin. Photograph: Lisi Niesner/Reuters A jubilant AfD co-leader, Tino Chrupalla, mocked Merz before his speech, saying voters had given his own party a “very clear result” and called on the chancellor to resign. About 2.5 million people were eligible to vote in Berlin and nearly 1.3 million in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania. The stinging blows from the latest elections had been expected to put pressure on Merz at a minimum to cede the CDU leadership, which would have in effect ruled out a run for re-election at the next national poll, due in 2029. Merz’s eroding support has created a sense of instability in Europe’s top economy, which is struggling with deindustrialisation, sluggish growth and soaring energy costs. If the AfD’s surge led Merz to abandon the chancellery prematurely, it would give the far right further momentum as France, Italy, Spain and Poland head into elections next year with nativist parties on the march . skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every day Sign up to Headlines Europe A digest of the morning's main headlines from the Europe edition emailed direct to you every week day after newsletter promotion Germany has high constitutional hurdles to replacing a chancellor against their will and any appointed successor would need to demonstrate a ruling majority. A failure to do so could trigger a new election. The AfD is the biggest opposition force in parliament and is leading national opinion polls with about 30%. It has called for Germany to quit the euro, end support for Ukraine and carry out mass deportations of “irregular” migrants, while citing the “destruction” of the CDU as one of its central goals. The CDU’s debacle in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania – a small, relatively poor state – is particularly bitter for Merz as it was home to the constituency of his arch-rival, Angela Merkel . While she governed Germany for 16 years, Merz appears to be on the ropes after no more than 16 months. View image in fullscreen Elif Eralp (centre), the candidate for Die Linke in Berlin, reacts to the projected results of the state election. Photograph: dts News Agency Germany/Shutterstock Merz took office in May 2025 at the helm of a coalition with the centre-left Social Democrats (SPD) promising to restore the German economy to strength and slash the AfD’s support. A failure to make decisive headway on either front has produced profound disappointment in his leadership, with only one in 10 Germans saying they are satisfied with his performance. An inability to connect with voters appears particularly marked in the former communist east , where the AfD is strongest. In Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, the Social Democratic party state premier, Manuela Schwesig, distanced herself during the campaign from a key pension change backed by her party in Merz’s coalition government. She was expected to hold on to power in a left-leaning coalition even if the AfD came out on top when all the votes were counted. Despite leading the polls for months, the far right failed to garner enough support to govern alone and the remaining parties have ruled out working with it. A confirmed win by Die Linke in Berlin, where the far-left party has called for expropriation of corporate landlords to fight rising housing costs, could see its candidate, Elif Eralp, become the capital’s first leader of Turkish origin. THE CANADIAN PRESS/Justin Tang Canada in talks with U.K. about merging defence financing institutions By Nick Murray, The Canadian Press Sep 16, 2026 | 11:55 AM The United Kingdom and Canada are talking about merging their proposed defence financing initiatives to amplify their effects, says a senior Canadian government official. The official, who was briefing reporters on background, says Ottawa is confident they’ll reach an agreement on bringing the two proposals together to form a joint institution, though that decision may not emerge from meetings this week. Read more: Europe wants Canada as its first ‘associate member’, von der Leyen tells Carney Carney wants private investors to run Canada’s four largest airports Carney’s investment summit draws protests by Indigenous leaders, eco groups, unions Prime Minister Mark Carney has championed the creation of a global Defence, Security and Resilience Bank to supply allies with low-cost borrowing for defence, and he’s enlisted support from eight countries, including Latvia, Luxembourg and Ukraine. The United Kingdom’s separate effort, called the Multilateral Defence Mechanism, is designed as a financing vehicle for joint purchases of military equipment and has won support from the Netherlands, Finland and Poland. Carney is stopping in Liverpool today for his first meeting with British Prime Minister Andy Burnham, who recently took office after Keir Starmer resigned over the summer. The government official says Carney has also been involved in a series of conversations about the Joint Expeditionary Force, a U.K.-led multinational Arctic security military coalition of which Canada is not a full member. Photograph: José Luis Magaña/AP US crime Mass shootings leave two people dead in Georgia and 12-year-old girl dead in Baltimore At least 25 injured at block party shooting in Georgia and three wounded in Baltimore park shooting, officials say Michael Sainato Sun 4 Oct 2026 11.23 EDT First published on Sun 4 Oct 2026 11.04 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Two people were killed and at least 25 others injured when a shooting erupted at a homecoming block party in Vienna, Georgia, early on Sunday, according to authorities. In another high-profile mass shooting in the US over the weekend, a 12-year-old girl was shot and killed and three others were wounded after gunfire evidently broke out over a parking spot in a Baltimore park on Saturday, officials said. The violence in Georgia occurred at a gathering of more than 1,000 people, local sheriff Craig Peavy told area news outlet WMAZ . Shots were fired at about 50 people in two locations about a block apart just after 1am on Sunday, Peavy told WMAZ. The pair killed at the scene were not immediately identified, and neither were suspects or a possible motive for the gunfire. Peavy added that about 25 people were taken to the hospital, as many as 35 people may have been wounded, and deputies were monitoring the crowd at the time of the shooting. Meanwhile, with respect to the shooting in Baltimore, police commissioner Richard Worley said two suspects were being sought after two different types of gun cartridges were found at the scene of the violence near a youth football event at Leon Day Park. “What we know is that there was some type of argument between two cowards, and of course they both opened fire on each other,” Worley said at a Saturday night news conference . “The dispute most likely occurred from a stupid parking spot, and they get into a fight, and the two cowards pull guns on each other.” Worley said the 12-year-old girl who was killed in that case was a bystander at a nearby field, who was hit when one of the shooters “fired multiple rounds down range”. A 25-year-old woman with the girl was shot, too. And so were two men, ages 23 and 28, according to police. None of the three wounded victims were believed to have life-threatening injuries, police said. The 12-year-old girl was pronounced dead at the scene, and paramedics took the woman to the hospital. The two other victims walked into a nearby hospital with injuries. “Two grown men got into an argument, and now a 12-year-old is gone,” the Baltimore mayor, Brandon Scott, said to reporters. “What happened out here today, is one of the most disgusting things I’ve ever seen in my life because that baby was just out here, at homecoming for this youth football league is out here every single day, trying to keep young people safe, trying to keep young men and young women on the right path.” There had been at least 355 mass shootings reported in the US so far for the year as of Sunday, which was the 277th day of 2026, according to the Gun Violence Archive . The archive, a nonpartisan reference resources, defines mass shootings as cases in which at least four victims are killed or wounded. The US perennially has high rates of such shootings, fueling calls from some quarters for more substantial federal gun control. But Congress has not passed such measures over the years. Photograph: Carl Court/Getty Images View image in fullscreen The victim’s commissioner said that the refusal of offenders to attend sentencing hearings compounded trauma. Photograph: Carl Court/Getty Images UK criminal justice Criminals who refuse to attend sentencing face losing prison privileges under new rules England and Wales judges to be able to keep inmates in cells for longer or stop visits if they refuse to face victims’ families in court Geneva Abdul Thu 22 Oct 2026 05.47 EDT First published on Thu 22 Oct 2026 03.54 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Offenders who refuse to face their victims’ families in court for sentencing could be stripped of privileges or kept in cells for weeks under government changes granting wider powers to judges in England and Wales. The imposition of new prison sanctions, coming into effect next year, builds on existing laws that order offenders to attend sentencing or face a fine or be jailed for a further two years for contempt of court. “Criminals should not be able to pick and choose when they face justice. Refusing to turn up to sentencing is an insult to victims and their families, and offenders must face the consequences,” said the prisons minister, Catherine McKinnell. The new rules, to be laid before parliament on Thursday, will grant judges new powers to impose a loss of prison privileges for 84 days, cell confinement for 21 days, a loss of social visits for 27 days and a restriction on visits to once every four weeks, for 84 days. They could result in offenders already facing decades behind bars facing additional punishments. The Ministry of Justice has said that while no measure can guarantee offenders will attend their sentencing hearing, the widened powers strengthen the consequences for offenders and ensure they can be “appropriately punished”. Younger offenders aged 18 to 20 could have privileges removed for up to 21 days or be confined to cells for up to 10 days, said the MoJ. Visitors from prisoners’ children will be exempt, to help maintain family ties and when in the child’s best interests. Claire Waxman, the victim’s commissioner for England and Wales, who has worked with relatives of the murder victims Sabina Nessa , Zara Aleena and Jan Mustafa, said the announcement reflected the “tireless efforts” of victims’ families. “I know how offenders’ refusal to attend sentencing hearings compounds trauma and robs families of one of the very few moments of accountability in the justice process,” said Waxman. “It is now essential that these powers are used consistently by courts and prisons, so families receive the justice and accountability they deserve.” skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to First Edition Our morning email breaks down the key stories of the day, telling you what’s happening and why it matters after newsletter promotion The move comes after nearly 2,000 prisoners across England and Wales were released from prison this month as part of a government plan to ease prison overcrowding.
